월요일.x: I go to school on Monday.

때.forms: noun + 때 (방학 때) · verb + -(으)ㄹ 때 (어릴 때)
때.x: I lived in Busan when I was young.
때.e: 어릴 때 = when I was young. Heads-up: 때 also means dirt or grime.
때.t: -(으)ㄹ 때 means 'when ~': 시간이 있을 때 = when I have time.

건너편.m: the other side, the opposite side (across)
건너편.x: There's a café across the street.
건너편.e: 건너다 (to cross) + 편 (side) — the side you'd cross over to.
건너편.t: Common phrase: 길 건너편 = across the street.

직업.x: What do you do for a living?
직업.t: Pronounced [지겁]. More polite question: 무슨 일을 하세요?

에어컨.ex: 너무 더워요. 에어컨 좀 켜 주세요.
에어컨.x: It's too hot. Please turn on the air conditioner.
에어컨.e: From English 'air con(ditioner)' — Koreans clip it; Americans would say AC.

음.x: Hmm, I'll go with the bibimbap.
음.e: Sound word for thinking, like English 'hmm'.
음.t: In texts it is written 음… or 흠. Don't confuse it with 음 (音) 'sound', as in 음악.

즐기다.x: On weekends, I relax and enjoy movies at home.
즐기다.e: Related to 즐겁다 'to be fun, joyful'.
즐기다.t: 즐겨 + verb means 'often, by preference': 즐겨 듣는 음악 'music I like to listen to.'

버리다.m: to throw away, to throw out; to abandon
버리다.ex: 이사하기 전에 오래된 옷을 모두 버렸어요.
버리다.x: Before moving, I threw away all my old clothes.
버리다.t: After another verb, -아/어 버리다 means 'completely' or 'unfortunately': 다 먹어 버렸어요 = I ate it all up.

찾아가다.m: to go to see, to visit (someone); to go looking for
찾아가다.x: During vacation I went to visit my grandmother in my hometown.
찾아가다.e: 찾다 'to look for' plus 가다 'go': go to find someone.

그래도.x: Even so, I like this job.
그래도.e: 그렇다 'to be so' + -아도 'even if' — 'even if that's so'.

우편물.ex: 제 우편물이 오면 경비실에 맡겨 주세요.
우편물.x: If any mail comes for me, please leave it at the security office.

당황하다.m: to be flustered, to be thrown off, to panic
당황하다.x: I was really flustered because I got a question out of nowhere.
당황하다.t: 당황하다 is being caught off guard, not shame; for shame use 창피하다.

시키다.m: to order (food); to make someone do, to tell someone to do
시키다.x: I was hungry, so I ordered chicken.
시키다.t: At restaurants 시키다 is the everyday word for 주문하다 'to order'; with people it means 'to make someone do'.

육체적.x: This work is very physically demanding.
육체적.t: Often paired with its opposite: 정신적으로나 육체적으로 'both mentally and physically'.

사투리.x: My grandmother still speaks her hometown dialect.
사투리.e: Native word for regional speech; the formal term is 방언.
사투리.t: Say 사투리를 쓰다 'to speak in dialect'. Standard Korean (표준어) is based on Seoul speech.

저출산.ex: 저출산 때문에 학교마다 학생 수가 줄고 있어요.
저출산.x: Because of the low birth rate, the number of students is falling at every school.
저출산.t: 저출산 고령화 is a fixed news phrase for Korea's population crisis.

칼로리.x: These snacks are way too high in calories.
칼로리.e: From English 'calorie'; note the double ㄹ sound: [칼로리].

도자기.x: Icheon is a city famous for its pottery.

정당.ex: 두 정당은 새 정책에 대해 서로 다른 의견을 가지고 있어요.
정당.x: The two parties have different opinions about the new policy.
정당.e: Literally 'political group'; don't confuse with 정당하다 'to be fair, just'.

끌어들이다.m: to drag in, to draw in, to involve; to attract (investment)
끌어들이다.x: Don't drag your friends into your own problems.
끌어들이다.e: 끌다 'pull' + 들이다 'bring in': pulling someone into a situation.
끌어들이다.t: Often negative, like dragging someone into trouble, but 투자를 끌어들이다 is neutral.

보태다.ex: 동생 학비에 제 월급을 조금 보탰어요.
보태다.x: I chipped in some of my salary for my younger sibling's tuition.
보태다.t: 힘을 보태다 means 'to lend a hand' or 'to pitch in'.

험하다.ex: 이 산은 길이 험해서 조심해야 해요.
험하다.x: The trails on this mountain are rough, so you need to be careful.
험하다.t: Also figurative: 험한 세상 'a harsh world', 말을 험하게 하다 'to talk nasty'.

시행착오.ex: 많은 시행착오를 겪은 후에 드디어 성공했어요.
시행착오.x: After a lot of trial and error, I finally succeeded.
시행착오.e: Literally 'trying it out and making mistakes'.

고시원.ex: 서울에 처음 왔을 때 고시원에서 살았어요.
고시원.x: When I first came to Seoul, I lived in a gosiwon.
고시원.e: Literally 'exam house' — originally tiny rooms for people studying for state exams.

계열사.m: affiliate, affiliated company (of a business group)
계열사.x: That group has more than 50 affiliates.

상응하다.m: to correspond to, to be commensurate with
상응하다.x: You should receive compensation that matches your effort.
상응하다.t: Usually N에 상응하는 N: 죄에 상응하는 벌 'a punishment that fits the crime.'

적반하장.m: the wrongdoer turning on the victim, the height of nerve
적반하장.ex: 자기가 잘못해 놓고 오히려 화를 내다니 적반하장이네요.
적반하장.x: He's the one who messed up, yet he's the one getting angry — what nerve.
적반하장.e: Literally 'the thief turns around and wields the club'.
적반하장.t: Often in 적반하장도 유분수지 'that's beyond the limit of nerve'.

매개체.x: Language is an important medium for passing on culture.
매개체.e: Literally 'go-between body': the thing that carries something across.

디스크.ex: 오래 앉아서 일하다가 허리 디스크에 걸렸어요.
디스크.x: I got a herniated disc in my lower back from sitting at work for long hours.
디스크.e: From English 'disk/disc'; Konglish surprise: in everyday talk it means a herniated disc.
디스크.t: Koreans say 디스크에 걸리다 or 디스크가 있다 to mean having a slipped disc.

순수 예술.ex: 그는 상업 미술보다 순수 예술에 관심이 많아요.
순수 예술.x: He's more interested in fine art than commercial art.
순수 예술.e: Literally 'pure art,' as opposed to commercial or applied art.

불기소.ex: 검찰은 증거 불충분으로 그 사건을 불기소 처분했습니다.
불기소.x: Prosecutors decided not to prosecute the case due to insufficient evidence.
불기소.e: Literally 'not raising a lawsuit' — prosecutors decline to bring charges.
불기소.t: Usually appears as 불기소 처분 'decision not to indict' in news reports.

경기부양.ex: 정부는 경기부양을 위해 대규모 예산을 투입했습니다.
경기부양.x: The government poured in a large budget to stimulate the economy.
경기부양.e: Literally 'lifting the economy's mood afloat'; 경기 means business conditions.
경기부양.t: 경기 'economy' and 경기 'game, match' are homonyms with different characters; context tells them apart.

감사원.m: Board of Audit and Inspection (Korea's national audit agency)
감사원.ex: 감사원은 정부 기관의 예산 사용을 감사합니다.
감사원.x: The Board of Audit and Inspection audits how government agencies use their budgets.
감사원.t: Don't confuse this 감사 (audit) with 감사 (thanks); context makes it clear.

의무론.ex: 칸트의 윤리학은 대표적인 의무론으로 알려져 있어요.
의무론.x: Kant's ethics is known as a classic example of deontology.
의무론.e: Literally 'duty theory'; -론 = theory or '-ism': 무신론, 결정론.

성욕.ex: 스트레스가 심하면 성욕이 줄어들 수 있습니다.
성욕.x: Severe stress can reduce sexual desire.

존엄사.m: death with dignity (by stopping life support)
존엄사.x: In Korea, death with dignity has been legally allowed since 2018.
존엄사.t: In Korea, 존엄사 usually means refusing life support, unlike 안락사, which actively ends life.

십이지장.ex: 검사해 보니 위와 십이지장에 궤양이 있대요.
십이지장.x: The tests showed I have ulcers in my stomach and duodenum.
십이지장.e: Literally 'twelve-finger intestine' — about twelve finger-widths long.

예술혼.x: Even while ill, the painter poured his whole soul into his art.
예술혼.e: Literally 'art soul': deep devotion to one's art.
예술혼.t: Often paired with burning verbs: 예술혼을 불태우다 (to pour one's soul into art).

연출가.ex: 연출가는 배우들과 함께 장면 하나하나를 다시 연습했어요.
연출가.x: The director rehearsed each scene again with the actors.
연출가.e: Literally 'one who brings out the performance'.
연출가.t: Theater uses 연출가; for films, 감독 is the usual word.

조선왕조실록.x: The Annals of the Joseon Dynasty were designated UNESCO Memory of the World in 1997.
조선왕조실록.e: Literally 'true records of the Joseon royal dynasty', written reign by reign.

등하불명.m: it's darkest under the lamp; missing what's right under one's nose
등하불명.ex: 등하불명이라더니 안경이 바로 책상 위에 있었네요.
등하불명.x: Talk about missing what's right in front of you — my glasses were right on the desk.
등하불명.e: Literally 'under the lamp it isn't bright.'
등하불명.t: The native proverb 등잔 밑이 어둡다 means the same and is more common in everyday speech.

종식하다.m: to end, to bring to an end, to put a stop to
종식하다.ex: 전 세계가 전쟁을 종식하기 위해 힘을 모았습니다.
종식하다.x: The whole world joined forces to bring the war to an end.
종식하다.e: Literally 'end and extinguish' — like a fire dying out.

톺아보다.m: to examine thoroughly, to comb through
톺아보다.ex: 이번 보고서에서는 사고의 원인을 하나하나 톺아봅니다.
톺아보다.x: This report examines the causes of the accident one by one.
톺아보다.e: 톺다 (to grope through every nook and gap) + 보다 (to look).
톺아보다.t: A revived native word, popular in media headlines as a pure-Korean alternative to 분석하다.

고색창연하다.m: time-honored, timeworn, with an antique look
고색창연하다.ex: 고색창연한 절이 산속에 조용히 자리하고 있어요.
고색창연하다.x: A timeworn old temple sits quietly in the mountains.

인과율.ex: 모든 일에는 원인이 있다는 인과율을 믿어요.
인과율.x: I believe in the law of causality: everything has a cause.

중층.ex: 이 소설은 중층적인 구조를 가지고 있어요.
중층.x: This novel has a multilayered structure.
